thinking: I'm going to check what mean_hidden actually refers to by comparing the mean of the layer-9 hidden states over the valid tokens (CLS and SEP included) against the mean_hidden_L9 from the second pass, for the same ids. After that I'll look at how often other tokens attend to CLS in each layer, and at a layer-0 CLS detector built from u = Σ⁻¹e, normalized, along with its leakage statistics.
Pass 3 is done; I'm checking whether mean_hidden includes the [CLS]/[SEP] tokens, measuring how much attention other tokens give [CLS] per layer, and then building the layer-0 [CLS] detector.

input.code:
meta = json.load(open('pass_3/meta.json')); print(meta.keys())
mask = np.load('pass_3/attention_mask.npy').astype(bool)
idx = np.arange(0,1024,16)
T9 = np.load('pass_3/token_hidden_L9.npy'); M9 = np.load('pass_2/mean_hidden_L9.npy')[idx]
m_all = np.array([T9[i][mask[i]].mean(0) for i in range(64)])
m_noss = np.array([T9[i][mask[i]][1:-1].mean(0) for i in range(64)])
print('diff incl', np.abs(m_all-M9).max(), 'diff excl', np.abs(m_noss-M9).max())
# attention to CLS by non-CLS tokens, per layer, per head
for l in range(1,13):
    A = np.load(f'pass_3/attention_L{l}.npy')
    vals=[]
    for i in range(64):
        n = mask[i].sum()
        vals.append(A[i,:,1:n,0].mean(1))  # heads x
    vals = np.array(vals).mean(0)
    sep=[]
    for i in range(64):
        n = mask[i].sum(); sep.append(A[i,:,1:n,n-1].mean(1))
    print(l, 'toCLS mean %.3f max head %.3f'%(vals.mean(), vals.max()), ' toSEP mean %.3f'%np.array(sep).mean())
